F1_fibrin_rich_tough.current_solution: NIMBUS geometric clot extractor (52.9% first-pass, 79.2% final with rescue)
F1_fibrin_rich_tough.still_fails: 20.8% of NIMBUS cases; aspiration fails because stiff clot doesn't deform into catheter
F1_fibrin_rich_tough.measurable_pre_intervention: PARTIALLY — RBC/fibrin ratio correlates with FPR failure (Vandelanotte 2024) but measured POST-retrieval

F2_sticky_adherent.description: Clot adheres to vessel wall, high friction
F2_sticky_adherent.current_solution: Cyclic aspiration, super-bore catheters — address clot-CATHETER friction, NOT clot-VESSEL adhesion
F2_sticky_adherent.still_fails: Clots with high vessel adhesion that cannot be overcome by aspiration or stent engagement
F2_sticky_adherent.measurable_pre_intervention: NO — clot-vessel friction not measured pre-intervention; ex vivo studies only

F3_calcified_hard.description: Clot contains calcium deposits, very rigid
F3_calcified_hard.current_solution: Balloon angioplasty (risky), rescue stenting (traps but doesn't remove)
F3_calcified_hard.still_fails: Heavily calcified clots that cannot be compressed or retrieved
F3_calcified_hard.measurable_pre_intervention: POTENTIALLY — NCCT can detect calcium, but calcified clot is rare

F4_fragmentable.description: Clot breaks apart during retrieval → distal emboli
F4_fragmentable.current_solution: Balloon guide catheters (flow arrest), distal filter devices
F4_fragmentable.measurable_pre_intervention: NO — clot cohesive strength not measured

F5_crossing_failure.description: Device cannot cross the occlusion to reach clot
F5_crossing_failure.still_fails: Very dense/long occlusions that no device can cross

F6_large_long.description: Clot too large for single-pass retrieval
F6_large_long.still_fails: Very long clots in tortuous vessels
F6_large_long.measurable_pre_intervention: YES — clot length measurable on CTA/MRA

aspiration_including_super_bore_cyclic.mechanism: Negative pressure ingests clot; cyclic reduces clot-catheter friction
aspiration_including_super_bore_cyclic.solves: Soft/round clots; addresses clot-CATHETER friction (not clot-VESSEL adhesion)
aspiration_including_super_bore_cyclic.still_fails: Stiff clots that don't deform; sticky clots with high vessel adhesion

rescue_stenting_balloon.mechanism: Stent traps clot against wall; balloon compresses
rescue_stenting_balloon.solves: Clots that cannot be retrieved but can be trapped/compressed
rescue_stenting_balloon.still_fails: Leaves clot in place (re-occlusion risk); requires dual antiplatelet therapy

adjunct_thrombolysis.still_fails: Delayed action; hemorrhage risk; cannot lyse fibrin-rich clots quickly

last_unsolved_physical_failure.evidence: No device measures or overcomes clot-VESSEL friction. Friction force review (SC-07) identifies this as 'critical'. All current devices address clot-DEVICE interaction (strut engagement, catheter ingestion, geometric clamping), NOT clot-VESSEL adhesion.
last_unsolved_physical_failure.key_distinction: Clot-CATHETER friction IS addressed (ROAR effect, cyclic aspiration). Clot-VESSEL adhesion is NOT addressed by any device.
last_unsolved_physical_failure.evidence: Clot composition measured POST-retrieval. No device characterizes clot type or adhesion BEFORE the first pass. Each failed pass INCREASES difficulty (SC-02: 'for every failed thrombectomy attempt, the clot became more difficult').

sharper_discovery_question.question: Can we know BEFORE the first pass which clot-vessel interaction is likely to defeat the planned thrombectomy strategy, and can we select a materially different physical action before causing additional passes and vessel injury?

P1_pre_intervention_adhesion_measurement.description: A device that PROBES clot-vessel adhesion before retrieval
P1_pre_intervention_adhesion_measurement.ce_012: PASSES — adhesion is a MECHANICAL property, not imaging recombination. Current imaging (CTA/MRI) shows location/size but NOT adhesion strength.
P1_pre_intervention_adhesion_measurement.ce_013: PASSES — clot-vessel adhesion is causally independent of existing measurements (function of clot composition + vessel wall + contact time)
P1_pre_intervention_adhesion_measurement.ce_014: APPLIED — searched 'clot adhesion', 'friction', 'vessel wall', 'separation'. No patent found for pre-intervention adhesion measurement.

P2_adhesion_breaking_mechanism.description: A mechanism that SEPARATES clot from vessel wall before retrieval
P2_adhesion_breaking_mechanism.ce_012: PASSES — no existing device breaks clot-vessel adhesion as primary mechanism (all PULL or ASPIRATE)
P2_adhesion_breaking_mechanism.ce_013: PASSES — adhesion-breaking is a new physical action, not a recombination
P2_adhesion_breaking_mechanism.ce_014: APPLIED — no patent found for clot-vessel adhesion breaking. ROAR/cyclic address clot-catheter friction, not clot-vessel.
P2_adhesion_breaking_mechanism.ce_015: NOT YET — needs force calculation (what force to break adhesion vs what current devices apply)

key_patents_found: US10722253B2: ROAR effect overcomes clot-CATHETER static friction (NOT clot-vessel)
US11464528B2: Waveform pressure reduces clot-CATHETER friction (NOT clot-vessel)
WO2017040681A1: Uses physiological adhesion to REMOVE clot (not break adhesion)
US20260102208A1: CT plaque characterization (imaging, not device-based adhesion)
no_patent_found_for: Clot-VESSEL adhesion breaking as primary mechanism
patent_landscape_ce_014.section_102: NOT ANTICIPATED — no single patent teaches clot-vessel adhesion measurement or breaking
patent_landscape_ce_014.section_103: NEEDS FULL ASSESSMENT — combination of friction studies + aspiration + imaging may be argued as obvious, but the specific step of SEPARATING clot from vessel wall before retrieval is not described in any combination

verdict.ce_012_ce_013: BOTH PASS for P1 and P2
verdict.ce_014: APPLIED — no direct patent hit for clot-vessel adhesion measurement/breaking
next_steps: 1. Article XX problem-existence gate: does clot-vessel adhesion actually cause retrieval failure? (Need evidence that adhesion — not just stiffness — is the failure mechanism)
2. CE-015 physics authority: what force is needed to break clot-vessel adhesion? Can a catheter-delivered device generate that force?
3. Full 12-stage patent attack on 'clot-vessel adhesion breaking' and 'pre-intervention adhesion measurement'
4. Decision-value: if adhesion could be measured/broken, would it change which device clinicians use or how many passes they attempt?
5. Identify the specific new technical primitive (what physical mechanism separates clot from vessel wall?)
verdict.mechanism_generation: BLOCKED — new domain identified but not yet explored
